title: Rapid client escalation cheat sheet - BeaconPay incident
content:
Purpose / quick goal:
- Put together a minimal, actionable playbook for the first 90 minutes of a BeaconPay customer escalation (prod latency + partial failures).
- Make it copy/pasteable for SRE + CS on-call; lightweight so an AE can read and share with the customer.

Top-level assumptions:
- Customer impacting: high-priority (P1).
- Symptoms: increased median latency to 1.2s from 120ms, 10-20% 5xx errors on generation endpoint.
- Region: us-west-2 primary.

Pre-call / pre-war-room checklist (5–10m)
- Create/confirm incident ticket: INFR-1427 (owner = Aarav).
- Start a Slack thread in #inc-beaconpay and DM pg leads: @rowan, @maya.
- Collect basic telemetry links: PROD dashboards (latency, 5xx), recent deploys (last 48h), capacity alarms.
- Set meeting invite for immediate 30-min war-room with video off by default unless needed.

Immediate roles (first 10m)
- Incident lead / comms: Aarav Singh — owns updates and customer-facing wording.
- SRE lead: Rowan Blake — triage root causes, coordinates mitigations.
- Serving runtime SME: Lena Ortiz — model-hosting/kv-cache checks, kernel selection status.
- CS / AE point: Maya Chen — mirrors customer expectations, collects downstream impact.
- Recorder: whoever joins first (annotate actions in ticket).

Initial triage script (10–25m)
- Confirm scope: which customers/users affected, specific routes (chat/gen/embed). Ask: is BeaconPay the only affected tenant or broad?
- Check deploys: any deployment in the last 48 hours to dedicated pools or shared infra? Link: deploys-dashboard.
- Metrics to screenshot: 1) token throughput, 2) p50/p95/p99 latencies, 3) 5xx rate by route, 4) queued requests per GPU.
- Quick checks (commands to run):
  - k8s: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep gpu-pool (check restarts)
  - logs: rlogs "service=inference AND tenant=beaconpay" --last 1h | head -n 200
  - model servers: curl http://model-host:9000/healthz (on each host)
  - cache hit rates: redwood-metrics query cache_kv_hit_rate{tenant="beaconpay"}

Short mitigations to try (ordered by low-risk first)
- Pin to fallback model variant (lower capacity footprint) for affected route — immediate rollback plan in case QoL drops. Owner: Lena, ETA 15m.
- Increase autoscale/burst capacity for BeaconPay pool (if Dedicated) — SRE check quota and runbook for reserved-capacity bursts. Owner: Rowan, ETA 10m.
- Temporary rate limit to protect core paths (reduce retries from client SDK). Communicate with AE. Owner: Maya, ETA 5m to notify customer.
- If KV cache warmup looks bad, trigger cache prewarm for top prefixes (script: tools/cache-prewarm --tenant beaconpay --top 200). Owner: Lena, ETA 20m.

Customer comms cadence (what to say, how often)
- First message (within 10m): "We've opened a high-priority incident investigating elevated latencies and error rates. Core engineering team engaged. We'll provide an update within 20 minutes."
- Subsequent updates: every 20 minutes or on significant milestone. Use consistent template: summary, impact, actions taken, ETA.
- If mitigation applied: include instructions for client: reduce concurrent requests during rollback window; share expected visible change.

Escalation thresholds (when to involve execs / infra on-call)
- If customer-facing errors >30% or latency >3s for >15m: page infra on-call and escalate to Director.
- If mitigation attempts fail twice or cannot be implemented within 30m: loop in SVP Eng.

Post-incident immediate actions (0–24h)
- Owner assigns postmortem lead within 2 business hours (ideally Aarav or Rowan).
- Collect artifacts: full logs, pcap for affected hosts (if applicable), traces for 1 hour before/after spike, deploy history, config diffs.
- Temporary remediation summary: what we did, why it reduced/had no effect, follow-ups required.
- Draft customer-facing root-cause (within 24h) even if initial is "under investigation".

Longer-term follow-ups (runbook / product changes)
- If autoscale or kernel selection is root cause: add canary to auto-deploy process + extra perf tests for tail latency.
- If model variant mismatch/quantization caused errors: add a model-compatibility gate in model catalog.
- Consider alert tuning: add a composite alert that triggers before p95 spikes by watching queue depth + 5xx trending.

Notes to self / reminders
- Keep the customer messaging simple; CS will reword but lead should sign off.
- Avoid promising ETA until mitigation shows partial improvement.
- Save screenshots in ticket and attach timeseries snippets (p95, p99).
- Remember to link any follow-up RFC/PRs in the postmortem.

Action items (first 3)
- Aarav: confirm incident ticket + first customer message (10m).
- Rowan: run pod/log checks + attempt burst capacity (15m).
- Lena: evaluate model variant rollback & cache warmup (20m).

Open questions (to answer during war-room)
- Is BeaconPay on Dedicated or Hosted? (if Dedicated, check quota + reserved GPU pool).
- Any recent config pushes to routing/policies?
- Are other tenants showing early warning signals?

Quick copy/paste template for first update to customer:
"Hi [AE/Customer], we've opened a high-priority investigation into increased latency and errors impacting your requests. Our SRE and serving teams are actively triaging. Next update in 20 minutes. Immediate mitigations being evaluated: temporary rate limiting, model variant pin, and autoscale burst. — Aarav (Incident Lead)"

Shelf items to convert to longer-term artifacts if recurring:
- Automated prewarm for top 1% prefixes by traffic per tenant.
- Canary profile for kernel selection changes that simulates tail-latency traffic.
- Tenant-level synthetic runner to detect early KV cache degradation.

End of scratchpad — keep iterative, update as the war-room progresses.
